key_insight: You can train autoregressive video diffusion models on short clips yet sample and infer over much longer videos by managing the generation history with a three-partition KV-cache that prevents linear cache growth and reduces temporal repetition and compounding errors.
problem_solved: Autoregressive video diffusion models suffer from intractable linear KV-cache growth, temporal repetition, and compounding errors when generating long videos; this work enables scalable long-video sampling and long-context inference without needing long-video training data.
method: Introduce a three-partition KV-cache strategy that separates history into: sink tokens (long-term preserved context), packed/summary tokens (compressed intermediate context), and active/recent tokens (sliding window for immediate generation).
Use a packing/forcing training procedure that exposes the model to short, concatenated segments so it learns to continue across packed boundaries and rely on the three-partition cache at inference.
At sampling/inference, maintain and update the three cache partitions to keep memory and compute manageable while reducing repetition and compounding errors during long-sequence generation.
impact: PackForcing makes long-video generation practical without long-video training, lowering memory and compute costs and producing more coherent long outputs—enabling researchers and practitioners to scale video diffusion models more efficiently.

paper_title: PackForcing: Short Video Training Suffices for Long Video Sampling and Long Context Inference
